featuredImage.alt: Visit Visa Extension Insurance in Saudi Arabia

contentHtml:
Saudi Arabia’s transformation into a global tourism and business hub has simplified entry for millions. However, staying beyond your initial visa period requires strict adherence to local laws. One of the most vital—yet often overlooked—steps is securing the correct visit visa extension insurance in Saudi Arabia.

In 2026, the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat) has made it clear: no insurance, no extension. At Connect Resources, we help individuals and corporations navigate these regulatory waters to ensure a seamless experience in the Kingdom.

1. Why Insurance is Mandatory for Visit Visa Extensions

The Saudi government, through the Council of Health Insurance (CHI), mandates that all visitors must have active health coverage. Insurance for visit visa extension Saudi Arabia is designed to cover:

  • Medical Emergencies: Immediate hospital care and surgeries.

  • Accidents: Treatment for injuries resulting from traffic or other incidents.

  • Repatriation: Costs associated with returning a patient or remains to their home country.

Without a valid policy that covers the entire duration of the extension, the Absher and Muqeem portals will automatically block your extension request.

2. Key Features of Insurance for Visit Visa Extension Saudi Arabia

In 2026, visit visa policies have been standardized to provide high-quality care. A typical policy approved for extension includes:

  • Maximum Coverage: Usually up to SAR 100,000.

  • Emergency Dental: Coverage for acute dental pain and basic repairs.

  • Pregnancy Emergencies: Critical care for unexpected maternal issues.

  • Inpatient Care: Coverage for hospital stays, including room charges (up to SAR 600/day).

3. How to Renew Insurance for Visit Visa Extension: 2026 Process

The days of visiting insurance offices are over. In 2026, the process of getting insurance for visit visa extension Saudi Arabia is entirely online.

Step-by-Step Guide:

  1. Check Eligibility: Ensure your current visa has not been expired for more than 3 days.

  2. Select a Provider: Visit an approved provider’s portal (like Tawuniya, Al Rajhi Takaful, or Bupa).

  3. Enter Details: You will need the Passport Number, Visa Number, and Border Number (the 10-digit number written by the immigration officer upon entry).

  4. Pay the Premium: Use Mada, Apple Pay, or credit card.

  5. Verify on CHI: The insurance provider will automatically upload the data to the Council of Health Insurance (CHI). You can verify this on their e-portal.

  6. Extend via Absher: Once the insurance is linked, log into Absher and complete the visa extension.

4. Top Insurance Providers in Saudi Arabia

For 2026, these are the most reliable providers for visit visa extension insurance in Saudi Arabia, known for their instant data syncing with government systems:

Provider Key Feature Average 30-Day Cost (SAR)
Tawuniya Largest network of hospitals. SAR 100 – 250
Al Rajhi Takaful Highly integrated with Al Rajhi Bank app. SAR 90 – 200
Arabian Shield Competitive pricing for long-term extensions. SAR 80 – 180
Bupa Arabia Premium service for high-end medical complexes. SAR 150 – 300

5. Cost Breakdown and Fees for 2026

Managing your budget for an extension involves more than just the insurance premium.

  • Visa Extension Fee: SAR 100 (standard for 30–90 days).

  • Insurance Premium: Varies based on age and duration (approx. SAR 50 – 300).

  • Late Penalty: SAR 500 (if you apply more than 3 days after your visa has expired).

Pro Tip: Always purchase your visit visa extension insurance in Saudi Arabia at least 48 hours before your visa expires to account for any data syncing delays between the insurance company and the Ministry of Interior.

6. Common Issues and How to Solve Them

Even with a digital system, errors can occur. Here is how to troubleshoot your insurance for visit visa extension Saudi Arabia:

  • “Insurance Not Found” on Absher: This usually means the provider hasn’t pushed the data to CHI. Check your status on the CHI website first; if it’s not there, contact your insurance provider’s WhatsApp support immediately.

  • Wrong Border Number: If the border number is incorrect in the insurance policy, the extension will fail. Double-check your entry stamp or the Absher “Visa Details” section before paying.

  • Age Limits: Some standard visit visa insurance policies have caps for visitors over 65 or 70. Ensure you select a specialized “Senior” policy if necessary.

7. How Connect Resources Saudi Supports You

Navigating the complexities of visit visa extension insurance in Saudi Arabia can be stressful for businesses managing international consultants or families hosting relatives. Connect Resources provides:

  • Group Insurance Management: Bulk renewals for corporate visitors and business delegations.

  • Compliance Advisory: Ensuring all your guests are 100% legal within the Kingdom’s 180-day stay limit.

  • PRO Services: We handle the manual “Jawazat” visits if a technical glitch prevents an online extension.

  • EOR Support: For those on short-term business assignments, we manage their entire legal presence, including all visa and insurance logistics.

8. Conclusion: Stay Legal, Stay Covered

The visit visa extension insurance in Saudi Arabia is your safety net. In 2026, it is the primary bridge to maintaining a legal status in the Kingdom. By choosing an accredited provider and ensuring your data is correctly synced, you can focus on enjoying the rich culture and booming business opportunities of KSA.

FAQ: Visit Visa Insurance in KSA

Q1: Can I use my international travel insurance for the extension?

No. For a legal visit visa extension in Saudi Arabia, you must use a Saudi-based insurance provider that is linked to the Council of Health Insurance (CHI) system.

Q2: Is COVID-19 coverage still required in 2026?

While the specific “COVID-19 Add-on” from previous years has been integrated into standard emergency care, your policy will still cover respiratory emergencies and hospitalizations related to viral infections.

Q3: Can I get a refund on my insurance if my visa extension is rejected?

Generally, insurance policies for extensions are non-refundable once issued and synced with the government system. However, some providers like Tawuniya may offer a partial refund if the visa has not yet been extended.

How to Verify Your Insurance Linkage: Step-by-Step Guide

Before attempting to extend your visa on Absher, you must ensure that your insurance data has been successfully transmitted to the government database. Follow these steps to perform a real-time verification on the Council of Health Insurance (CHI) portal.

Step 1: Access the Official CHI Portal

Go to the official website of the Council of Health Insurance: www.chi.gov.sa.

  • Select the “E-Services” tab from the top menu.

  • Click on “Inquiry about Visitor, Tourist, or Pilgrim Insurance Status.”

Step 2: Enter Your Credentials

You will be prompted to provide one of the following to identify your policy:

  • Passport Number (The most reliable method for visitors).

  • Visa Number (Available on your visa grant notice).

  • Border Number (The 10-digit number handwritten by immigration at the airport).

Step 3: Verification Code (Captcha)

Enter the security code displayed in the image to confirm you are not a bot. Click “OK” or “Search.”

Step 4: Review Your Status

The system will display your insurance details. For a successful visa extension, pay attention to these three fields:

  • Insurance Company: Verify it matches your chosen provider (e.g., Tawuniya, Bupa).

  • Policy Status: It must show as “Active” or “Valid.”

  • Policy Expiry Date: The date must cover the new duration you are requesting for your visa.

Pro-Tip for 2026: If the CHI portal shows your insurance as active but Absher still gives an error, wait 1 to 2 hours. The data synchronization between the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Interior can sometimes have a slight lag.
